report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Critical review finding: a cancelled memory call loses its error and its outcome is never logged)

This PR is not ready to merge: one reviewer found that when a memory tool call is cancelled after its store work has started, the store work's error is dropped and nothing is logged, which the code ran on the event loop did not do.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

1. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 88–99 (`run_memory_call`): when the task awaiting `loop.run_in_executor(...)` is cancelled after the store call has started, asyncio drops the worker's result or exception, and `concurrent.futures` never logs an exception that nobody retrieved. A failing `delete_memory`, `clear_memories` or `import_memory` baseline call (`clear=True`) whose caller was cancelled therefore loses its error: the handler's `logger.exception` at `server.py` lines 599–603 and 623–627 has already exited with `CancelledError`. A successful delete or wipe in the same situation also leaves no log line. Before this change the call ran on the loop and could not be interrupted, so its error reached the handler. The repository's SQL pool handles the same case in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py` lines 119–122 and 157 with `future.add_done_callback(_log_call_after_cancel)`; the memory worker has no equivalent, and the new tests check only the ordering of a cancelled delete, not its outcome. (raised by 1/6 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 80–99: one worker with an unbounded queue means a hung ChromaDB call makes every later memory tool call wait forever, with no timeout, no error to the caller and no log line saying the queue is stuck. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 121 documents the trade-off, but the SQL pool in `sql_threads.py` warns when all slots are busy and fails a call that waits too long for a slot. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 95–99: a `run_memory_call` made from code already running on the memory worker deadlocks, and only the docstring guards against it; no thread-name check or error detects it. No current path does this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 70–99: the "never overlap, never on the loop" rule depends on every caller remembering to use `run_memory_call`. The synchronous `MemoryStore` methods (`iter_all`, `clear`, `get_all`, `iter_records`, `get_one`, `delete_ids`), the `memory.admin` functions that call them and `exporter.py` lines 41 and 47 remain directly callable from the loop; only the call sites in `server.py` (542, 566, 591, 620, 695, 729) and `importer.py` line 76 and the tests hold the rule in place. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 70–73: the comment says one worker keeps the synchronous calls from running at the same time, including ChromaAgentMemory's lazy unlocked client and collection creation. But `ChromaAgentMemory._get_client` and `_get_collection` (`agent_memory.py` lines 135–175) are also called from ChromaAgentMemory's own two-thread executor (`_save`, `_delete`, `_clear`, searches), which can run at the same time as the memory worker. The single worker serializes only `run_memory_call` calls among themselves. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 34 repeats the same reason. This is not a regression: the earlier on-loop design had the same exposure. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: code comment only; making it true changes no output or branch; git grep —no-index of view-head for "lazy unlocked client" printed only store.py:71; the comment is never printed to users -->
5. `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` lines 308–310: the comment "One add + one import item, each normalized on the loop; the store baseline normalizes the stored rows on the worker." sits above `assert len(threads["dumps"]) == 7` but describes the `dedup` count asserted at line 313 (`== 3`). It also does not explain the 3: a SQL pair's dedup key normalizes `question` and `sql` separately (two calls) plus one for the schema doc (`importer.py` lines 83 and 90). (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: test comment only; git grep —no-index of view-head for "One add + one import item" printed only the test file line 308; no tool or agent reads it; never published -->
6. `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` lines 283–310: exact-count and exact-set assertions make the new tests brittle. Line 310 counts every `json.dumps` in `server.py`; line 283 replaces `server_module.json` with a `SimpleNamespace` holding only `dumps`; line 223 fixes the set of store methods the overlap test sees; and `_SYNC_STORE_METHODS` (line 49) is a hand-kept list, so a synchronous `MemoryStore` method added later would not be checked by the off-loop test. None of these lets a regression through today. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No call to a synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method made by an MCP tool registered under `memory.allow_admin_tools` or `memory.allow_import` runs on the event-loop thread. A test records the thread each such call runs on, for every one of those tools, and asserts it is not the thread running the event loop.
- [ ] While a memory tool's store call is held open, `GET /healthz` on the same HTTP server returns 200 within 2 seconds, measured by a 2-second httpx request timeout as in `tests/integration/test_slow_agent_run_responsiveness.py`. Once released, the held tool call returns its normal, non-error result.
- [ ] Within one server process, synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method calls made for two different calls of those MCP tools are never in progress at the same time. This holds even when the tool call that started one is cancelled while it runs: the next such call starts only after the cancelled call's store work returns.
- [ ] For the same store contents and arguments, with no write other than the call's own overlapping it and no cancellation of the call, each of those MCP tools returns the same result as before the change, including each `isError` result and message. That covers, at minimum, a memory that is not found, a corrupt store, invalid input, a lossy export, an add or import with failed items, and a generic store failure. A `list_memories` call whose store reads a managed write (a write inside `CollectionState.writing()`) overlaps returns an `isError` result whose text contains `Memory store changed during listing; retry the request.` and never a partial listing. The existing memory tool tests pass without changes to their assertions.
- [ ] The CLI `import-memory` command reports the same saved, duplicate and error counts and exit status as before for the same store and bundle, including with `--clear` and `--dry-run`.
- [ ] The change leaves `add_memories`' per-item validation, `import_memory`'s parsing of its bundle JSON, `import_bundle`'s per-item de-duplication check of the incoming items, and each handler's final `json.dumps` of the object its `memory.admin` function returns running on the event loop.
